note_on_task_packet: The retention module is services/telemetry/heartbeat_retention.py (not retention.py); services/telemetry/test_retention.py does not exist, the retention tests are in test_heartbeat_retention.py.

change.digest: paper_runtime._state_change_digest drops volatile keys recursively (attempted_at, staged_at, pair_id, state_digest, event_id, sequence_no/seq/seq_no and any key ending _at, _ts, _timestamp, _sequence) before hashing performance_telemetry + member_virtual_books.
change.rate_limit: A change whose structural digest (status, code, fill_count, positions, send flags; per member book: identity, fills, fill_gaps, underlyings, marks_complete) is unchanged is mark-to-market-only and is sent at most PANTHEON_RUNTIME_STATE_SNAPSHOT_MTM_MAX_PER_HOUR (default 4) per runtime per hour. A structural change (fill, position, member book) is sent at the next tick.
change.heartbeat: _maybe_emit_heartbeat gate and last-emit update are now atomic under a lock.
change.retention: heartbeat_retention deletes runtime_state_snapshot rows older than PANTHEON_TELEMETRY_STATE_SNAPSHOT_RETENTION_DAYS (default 3) in bounded batches, keeping the newest and oldest snapshot per runtime and snapshots with performance_telemetry.status in marks_unavailable, invalid_ledger, invalid_drawdown_series.

heartbeat_explanation_289_to_308_per_hou.code_bound: A single process cannot exceed 240/hour: the gate needs >= 15 s since the last accepted emit (full-hour replay test: 239-240 heartbeats).
heartbeat_explanation_289_to_308_per_hou.cause_found_in_code: The gate was check-then-act with no lock and the last-emit time was written only after the HTTP emit returned. The drain loop (1 s poll) and the dedicated heartbeat thread both call it, so while one thread was inside a slow emit the other passed the same gate. test_concurrent_heartbeat_callers_emit_once_per_interval fails without the lock and passes with it. Snapshots ride the same tick, which is why hosted snapshots (286-304/h) track hosted heartbeats (289-308/h).
heartbeat_explanation_289_to_308_per_hou.not_verified: I could not measure hosted. Whether the race alone accounts for the whole 20-28 percent excess, or a second process / pre-fix release was also running, must be confirmed on hosted after deploy by counting heartbeats per runtime per hour (expect <= 240).

runtime_budget_replay.shape: one runtime, 24 h, 1 s poll, 15 s heartbeat interval; 17 h flat pre/post-market (only attempted_at/pair_id change), 7 h with pnl changing every second and a fill every 3000 s. Event JSON bytes from the replay fake emitter; hosted rows are about 610 bytes (member books) vs about 506 here.
runtime_budget_replay.pre_open_hour: 1 snapshot (the start snapshot) per runtime in the first hour, 0 after
runtime_budget_replay.after_hard_cap: start + structural changes + 4 mtm-only per hour => at most about 100 per runtime per day before structural changes

rollback: runtime_summary.py is unchanged and already folds snapshot and heartbeat state carriers by last state; the previous release reads the reduced stream (test_rollback_release_summarises_reduced_snapshot_stream) and the retained rows (test_summary_unchanged_when_retention_keeps_oldest_newest_and_unknown_status_snapshots). Retention only deletes rows; env flag PANTHEON_TELEMETRY_STATE_SNAPSHOT_RETENTION_DAYS can be raised to stop deletion. Deleted rows are not recoverable.
tests: services/telemetry/test_heartbeat_retention.py (test_runtime_state_snapshot_retention_keeps_latest_and_summary_inputs rebuilds the summary from Postgres before and after deletion and compares equal)
